raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #43184.

`SGLDLoraLoader.load_lora` clones the model, adds the new LoRA to the clone's `patches`, and sends every patch on the clone to `set_lora`, but it returned the original `model`. A chained second LoRA node therefore never saw the first LoRA and called `set_lora` with only its own. The worker's `LoRAPipeline.set_lora` applies with `clear_existing=True`, replacing the active set, so every LoRA but the last was silently dropped (and only the last is re-applied after a worker reload).

## Modifications

- `load_lora` returns the patched clone (`bi`). `SGLDModelPatcher.clone` keeps the same executor, wrappers, options and `model_type`, so nothing downstream changes except that the next LoRA node now sees this one.
- `test/unit/test_comfyui_lora_node.py`: imports the real `nodes.py` (ComfyUI modules stubbed under `mock.patch.dict(sys.modules)`), chains two LoRA nodes, and checks that the last `set_lora` call carries both LoRAs and that the upstream model is not mutated.

## Accuracy Tests

Two real `SGLDLoraLoader` nodes chained on a real `SGLDModelPatcher` (ComfyUI master 58b176f), with the resulting calls fed into the real `LoRAPipeline.set_lora` (set up like `test_lora_pipeline.py`, identity base layer, `style` adds to output[0], `detail` to output[1], input `[1, 1]`):

```
before: set_lora calls [['style'], ['detail']]           -> active=['detail'],          output=[1.0, 2.0]
after:  set_lora calls [['style'], ['style', 'detail']]  -> active=['style', 'detail'], output=[2.0, 2.0]
```

Unit tests (CPU):

```
before fix: 1 failed   test_comfyui_lora_node.py   (assert ['detail'] == ['style', 'detail'])
after fix:  107 passed, 11 skipped (CUDA only), 3 xfailed   test_comfyui_{lora_node,session,adapters,h3,generator,profile}.py, test_conditioning_cache.py, test_lora_pipeline.py
            12 passed   apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/test/test_h3_request.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (not needed)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (not applicable)

Added test_switching_and_dropping_loras_sends_exact_active_set. It covers a chain that stops early, switching to a different chain from the same base, going back to an earlier chain, and re-applying a nickname with a new strength. set_lora gets exactly the active set each time and no branch leaks into the base. Passes on Modal.

LGTM. Returning the patched clone preserves the adapter set across chained nodes. The added regression covers switching branches, reducing the active set and replacing a nickname's strength without mutating the base. Requesting the targeted CI file on this head.

files.patch:
@@ -78,6 +78,56 @@ def test_chained_lora_nodes_keep_every_lora() -> None:
     assert set(second.patches) == {"style", "detail"}
 
 
+def test_switching_and_dropping_loras_keeps_exact_set_per_branch() -> None:
+    nodes = _load_nodes()
+    calls = []
+    executor = SimpleNamespace(set_lora=lambda **kwargs: calls.append(kwargs))
+    base = _Model(executor)
+    loader = nodes.SGLDLoraLoader()
+
+    def names(model):
+        return model.model_options["sgld_lora_input"]["lora_nickname"]
+
+    def strengths(model):
+        return model.model_options["sgld_lora_input"]["strength"]
+
+    (a,) = loader.load_lora(base, "a.safetensors", 1.0, nickname="a")
+    (ab,) = loader.load_lora(a, "b.safetensors", 0.5, nickname="b")
+    (abc,) = loader.load_lora(ab, "c.safetensors", 0.7, nickname="c")
+    assert names(abc) == ["a", "b", "c"]
+
+    # Reducing: a branch that stops after "a" carries only "a".
+    (a2,) = loader.load_lora(base, "a.safetensors", 1.0, nickname="a")
+    assert names(a2) == ["a"]
+
+    # Switching: a different chain from the same base drops the earlier ones.
+    (xy,) = loader.load_lora(
+        loader.load_lora(base, "x.safetensors", 1.0, nickname="x")[0],
+        "y.safetensors",
+        0.3,
+        nickname="y",
+    )
+    assert names(xy) == ["x", "y"]
+    assert strengths(xy) == [1.0, 0.3]
+
+    # Going back to an earlier chain restores exactly its set.
+    (ab_d,) = loader.load_lora(ab, "d.safetensors", 1.0, nickname="d")
+    assert names(ab_d) == ["a", "b", "d"]
+
+    # Re-applying the same nickname replaces its strength, not duplicates it.
+    (a3,) = loader.load_lora(abc, "a.safetensors", 0.2, nickname="a")
+    assert names(a3) == ["a", "b", "c"]
+    assert strengths(a3) == [0.2, 0.5, 0.7]
+
+    # Loader nodes never touch the shared worker, and no branch leaked into
+    # the shared base or its siblings.
+    assert calls == []
+    assert base.patches == {} and "sgld_lora_input" not in base.model_options
+    assert names(a) == ["a"] and names(ab) == ["a", "b"]
+    assert set(a.patches) == {"a"} and set(ab.patches) == {"a", "b"}
+    assert set(a2.patches) == {"a"} and set(xy.patches) == {"x", "y"}
+
+
 class _TupleLinear(torch.nn.Linear):
     def forward(self, x):
         return super().forward(x), None
